messages:
oncall-bot: PAGING: S2 — single-tenant tail latency spike for customer evergro in s-eu-prod. Detected p99 streaming latency = 8.4s (SLO p99 <= 2s). Affected: streaming/generative realtime APIs for ~12% of requests. Pager rotation: maya -> sven. Please acknowledge.

maya: ack — I'm up. looking at dashboards now. linking perf panel: https://graf.redwood/evergro/streams (p95/p99 panels).

maya: quick snapshot: p95 ~1.9s, p99 ~8.4s, error rate small but clients report streaming stalls (clients hang waiting for final chunk). CPU on dedicated pool nodes at 60-70%, GPU util fine.

eli: digging into runtime logs — I see a pattern of repeated full KV-cache misses for long prefixes. lots of requests with >20k token prompt prefixes (customer has long history import). KV cache eviction/repin churn spikes.

eli: tail of logs: ```
2026-03-14T00:21:04Z WARN kv_cache: miss for prefix_id=evr-9ab size=21432
2026-03-14T00:21:04Z INFO model: start_stream session=evr:session:123 host=gpu-23
2026-03-14T00:21:11Z ERROR stream: stall detected 6400ms waiting for tokens
```

maya: interesting — this matches reports. high-concurrency sessions + unusually long prefixes causing cache thrash + batching delays. Could be head-of-line blocking in continuous batching.

ingrid: any correlation with recent rollout? we pushed minor kernel/attention patch to s-eu-prod ~1:30 UTC yesterday. ops checks green but maybe interaction with long-prefix paths.

eli: I don't see increased crash rates or OOMs tied to that deploy. Kernel selector path seems fine. Problem looks workload-specific.

maya: mitigation plan (short): 1) route heavy evergro sessions to rdx-medium (lower mem -> short-prefix-friendly streaming path) 2) enable prefix-clip at 8k tokens for this tenant temporarily 3) increase dedicated worker count for evergro pool by +2.

sven: taking over (oncall handoff). ETA 5m to apply routing and prefix clip. will run traffic-split 10/90 to verify.

ops-bot: ACTION triggered by sven: route-split create --customer evergro --from s-eu-prod --to shared-eu --weight 10 --model rdx-medium

maya: running a quick canary:```
$ redwood route set --customer evergro --pool shared-eu --model rdx-medium --weight 10
Applied route split id=rs-evr-431
```

eli: also pushing a temporary KV-config tweak: increase cache size for evergro pool and bump hold-time to reduce churn. Command:```
$ redwood admin kv-config update --pool evergro-pool --max-entries 500000 --hold-ms 600000
```

maya: monitoring p99 after canary — current canary traffic shows p99 down to 2.3s for that subset. Not perfect but big improvement.

customer-success: pinged evergro support channel — asked them to pause bulk history imports and to confirm client-side retries/backoffs. they said they can postpone sync for 2 hours.

ingrid: good catch on pref-lengths. we should keep prefix-clip at 8k for now and run stress test with synthetic long-history sessions in staging.

sven: increasing worker count now +2 on evergro dedicated pool. ```
$ redwood infra scale --pool evergro-pool --replicas +2 --reason "tail latency mitigation"
```

ops-bot: scale job accepted, nodes provisioning (estimated 90s).

maya: after scale + canary + kv-config tweak, cluster p99 (tenant aggregated) dropped to ~2.1s within 3m. Streaming stalls reduced, client timeouts no longer seen in canary.

eli: logs show KV miss rate down 70% for canary traffic. batch formation latency reduced from 120ms -> 30ms on canary.

sven: rolling canary 10 -> 50 -> 100 over next 10m. watching p95/p99 and stream stall metric. if any regressions rollback route-split.

maya: recording steps and RCA notes. likely root cause: combination of incoming long-prefix tokens per request + high concurrency from single tenant, triggering KV cache eviction thrash and longer batch waits that amplified into streaming stalls. interaction with kernel selector patch unlikely but will run targeted tests.

eli: follow-ups: - add tenant-level prefix-length guardrail at routing layer - improve KV cache telemetry per-tenant - add automated routing fallback for tail-latency > threshold

customer-success: evergro confirmed improved UX on their end. they didn't see timeouts after 5m. asked for postmortem and timeline.

sven: final: rolling to 100% completed at ts=1976543550. I'll keep monitoring until 1976544200. handing post to maya (RCA lead).

on-message: reaction :thumbsup: from maya, eli, ingrid.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated, severity downgraded to S3, monitoring.

maya: thanks team — documenting detailed RCA and action items now. will create incident postmortem and link here.

sven: thanks, I'm out.
